Neither smut type matches. 

**Summary of observations:**
- Test image: Cross-section of a corn ear/cob
- Tan/cream kernels around the outer ring
- **Pink to reddish-purple discoloration** throughout the internal cob tissue and vascular areas
- Some powdery/dusty tan material in the center

**Reasoning:**
- Common smut / Head smut: No — those show galls or black spore masses, not pink cob cross-sections
- Diplodia ear rot: White mold at base — no pink coloration
- Aspergillus/Trichoderma: Olive-green or dark green external kernel mold — no match
- Fusarium ear rot: White to salmon cottony mold on scattered kernels — not this pattern
- **Ear_rots_Gibberella**: Pinkish-white to pink-red coloration from Fusarium graminearum infection. The internal cob cross-section showing pink-red discoloration of the vascular and pith tissue is a classic diagnostic feature of Gibberella ear rot when the cob is cut open. The uniform pink/reddish-purple staining throughout the internal tissue matches this.
